problems.title: The last of n consecutive integers
problems.question: The smallest of n consecutive integers is m. Find the largest.
problems.idea: There are n-1 increments from first to last.
steps: The first term uses zero increments.
The nth term therefore uses n-1 increments.

problems.title: Integer values of a rational expression
problems.question: How many integer n make (5n²+2n+3)/n an integer?
problems.idea: Separate the integer part from 3/n.
steps: For integer n, the expression is integral exactly when n divides 3.
The divisors are -3,-1,1,3.

problems.title: Remaining travel at double speed
problems.question: A traveller covers 3/8 of a route in 6 hours, then doubles the speed. How long for the remaining route?
problems.idea: Compare the remaining distance with the first part, then divide by the speed multiplier.
steps: The remaining-to-first distance ratio is (5/8)/(3/8)=5/3.
At the original speed it would take 6·5/3=10 hours. At twice the speed it takes 5.

problems.title: A radical quotient with a maximum at zero
problems.question: For which x is $(\sqrt x-\sqrt2)/(x-2)$ largest?
problems.idea: Cancel using the conjugate while retaining the original excluded point.
steps: The domain is x≥0,x≠2. The quotient equals 1/(√x+√2).
The denominator is smallest at x=0 and increases with x.
Thus the maximum is 1/√2, attained at x=0.

problems.title: Opposite sides of a line use opposite signs
problems.question: The pictured A,B lie on opposite sides of a line, at distances 20 and 16 cm. Find the midpoint’s distance.
problems.idea: Signed distance changes linearly along a segment.
steps: Use signed distances +20 and -16.
Their average is 2, whose absolute value is 2.
problems.note: If both endpoints were on the same side the distance would be 18 cm; the original diagram places them on opposite sides.

problems.title: A negative slope through the origin
problems.question: Which quadrants contain y=(1-√2)x?
problems.idea: The coefficient is negative.
steps: For x>0, y<0, giving quadrant IV.
For x<0, y>0, giving quadrant II.
The origin is on the graph but belongs to no quadrant.

problems.title: Scaling a negative power
problems.question: x=(5/9)n²n⁻⁷. How does x change if n is multiplied by 6?
problems.idea: Combine powers of n first.
steps: The new value is 1/6⁵ times the old one.
Since 6⁵=7776, x is divided by 7776.

problems.title: Bisect a base angle of an isosceles triangle
problems.question: In ABC, AB=BC, B=40°, and AD bisects A. Find ∠ADC.
problems.idea: First identify the equal base angles.
steps: A=C=70°, and CAD=35°.
In triangle ADC, the remaining angle is 180°-70°-35°=75°.

problems.title: Perimeter of a tangential isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid circumscribes a radius-12 circle. Its acute base angle has sine 0.8. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: The circle diameter is the trapezoid height.
formulas: h=2R; leg=h/sinα; in a tangential trapezoid the base sum equals the leg sum.
steps: h=24, so each leg is 24/0.8=30.
The base sum is 60, equal to the two-leg sum.
The perimeter is 60+60=120.

problems.title: A square is a special rhombus
problems.question: How many symmetry axes does a rhombus have?
problems.idea: Separate the ordinary rhombus from its square special case.
formulas: A rhombus is symmetric in both diagonals; a square also has two side-midpoint axes.
steps: Every non-square rhombus has exactly its two diagonal symmetry axes.
If the rhombus is a square, it has four.
problems.answer: 2 for a non-square rhombus; 4 if it is a square.
problems.note: The question does not exclude a square. Under the inclusive definition of rhombus, both cases must be distinguished.

problems.title: A raft moves at the current speed
problems.question: A boat takes 9 hours downstream and 12 hours upstream over the same distance. How long does a raft take?
problems.idea: Subtract the two effective speeds.
steps: Subtract to get 2u=D(1/9-1/12)=D/36.
Thus u=D/72, and raft time D/u=72 hours.

problems.title: Several listed piece counts are possible
problems.question: Start with one sheet. Each cut replaces one piece by four. Which of 18,17,19,13,22 pieces can result?
problems.idea: Each operation adds exactly three pieces.
formulas: After k cuts the number is 1+3k.
steps: Possible counts are 4,7,10,13,16,19,22,… after the initial cut.
19,13,22 are all congruent to 1 modulo 3 and are obtained after 6,4,7 cuts respectively.
18 and 17 have the wrong remainders.
problems.note: This multiple-choice question has three correct choices, rather than one.

problems.title: Area of a right trapezoid
problems.question: In right trapezoid ABCD, AD+BC=20, AB+CD=18, D=30°. Find its area.
problems.idea: The vertical leg is h and the sloping leg is twice h.
steps: CD=2h and AB=h, so 3h=18 and h=6.

problems.title: Two roots with a bound on squared roots
problems.question: Find q so x²-6x+q=0 has two real roots whose squared sum is less than 26.
problems.idea: Combine the discriminant and Vieta’s formulas.
steps: The squared-sum condition gives q>5.
Two distinct real roots require q<9.
Thus 5<q<9. If a double root counts as two roots with multiplicity, q=9 also qualifies.
problems.answer: (5,9) for two distinct roots; (5,9] if multiplicity is counted.
problems.note: The printed choice uses distinct roots. The endpoint q=9 depends on what “two roots” means.

problems.title: Cancel a cubic factor
problems.question: Evaluate $\dfrac{X+1}{X^2+X+1}\div\dfrac1{X^3-1}$ at $X=3\sqrt2$.
problems.idea: Division by a reciprocal multiplies by its denominator.
steps: The expression reduces to (X+1)(X-1)=X²-1.
At X=3√2, X²=18, giving 17.

problems.title: Combine roots with a common sixth-root index
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt[3]{2\sqrt5}\sqrt[6]{16/5}$.
problems.idea: Write the cube root as a sixth root.
steps: The product is the sixth root of (2√5)²·16/5=20·16/5=64.
Since 2⁶=64, the positive sixth root is 2.

problems.title: Half a minute faster over one kilometre
problems.question: A car travels at 60 km/h. By how much must its speed rise to cover 1 km half a minute faster?
problems.idea: Convert the original travel time first.
steps: At 60 km/h, 1 km takes 1 minute. The new time is 1/2 minute=1/120 hour.
The new speed is 120 km/h.
The required increase is 120-60=60 km/h.

problems.title: Four real roots from a quadratic substitution
problems.question: Find the sum of the roots of $7/[(x+3)(x-2)]+4/[(x+4)(x-3)]=1$.
problems.idea: Both denominators depend on u=x²+x.
formulas: The denominators are u-6,u-12; exclude x=-4,-3,2,3.
steps: Multiplying on the domain gives 7(u-12)+4(u-6)=(u-6)(u-12), hence u²-29u+180=0.
Thus u=9 or u=20. The two equations x²+x=9 and x²+x=20 each have two real roots, with sum -1 each.
No root makes u equal to the excluded values 6 or 12. The combined root sum is -2.

problems.title: A diameter bound and a right-triangle special case
problems.question: A triangle inscribed in the pictured circle has longest side ML=9. Which listed circumferences are possible: 9.4π,9π,8π,7π,6π?
problems.idea: A chord cannot exceed the diameter.
steps: Since a=9, the circumference must be at least 9π, eliminating 8π,7π,6π.
For an acute largest angle A, sinA is between √3/2 and 1, so 9π<C≤6√3π. The value 9.4π is attainable.
The value 9π is also attainable by a right triangle with hypotenuse ML=9, since ML is then a diameter.
problems.answer: 9.4π is possible. Also 9π is possible if a right triangle is allowed.
problems.note: The drawing appears acute but has no right-angle exclusion in the text. Treating an unmarked sketch as an acute-angle condition would hide the second valid possibility.

problems.title: A right triangle cut by a line
problems.question: In the pictured triangle, K=(0,1), M is the y-intercept of y=2x-4, and KL is horizontal to that line. Find its area.
problems.idea: Read the two perpendicular leg lengths.

problems.title: Convert 129 to binary
problems.question: Write 129 in base 2.
problems.idea: Use powers of two.
steps: The bits for positions 7 and 0 are 1, and all six intervening bits are 0.
Thus the binary representation is 10000001.

problems.title: Equal opposite parallelogram angles
problems.question: The diagram labels opposite angles (x-5)° and (y+10)°, with x+y=195°. Find x.
problems.idea: Opposite interior angles are equal.
steps: Thus x-y=15. Add this to x+y=195.

problems.title: Undo the input transformation
problems.question: The only roots of f(x)=0 are 1,-2. Find the roots of f(-2x)=0.
problems.idea: The new argument must equal an original root.
steps: The first equation gives x=-1/2.
The second gives x=1.

problems.title: A product in a negative open interval
problems.question: For 0<x≤4 and -12<y<0, which of 0,-48,-20π,π,-2π can equal xy?
problems.idea: The product is strictly negative and greater than -48.
steps: Only -2π lies in this interval.
It is attainable, for example x=1,y=-2π, satisfying all given bounds.

problems.title: A perfect cube in scientific notation
problems.question: Which is a positive integer cube: 2.7·10¹¹,2.7·10¹³,2.7·10¹⁴,2.7·10¹⁵,2.7·10¹⁸?
formulas: An integer cube has every prime exponent divisible by 3.
steps: The powers of 2 and 5 in 27·10ᵏ⁻¹ are both k-1.
Only k=13 gives k-1 divisible by 3 among the listed exponents.

problems.title: Bound the longer rectangle side
problems.question: A rectangle’s longer side is 7 cm greater than the other and its area is below 60 cm². Which proposed longer side is impossible: 8,8.5,7.5,11.5,12.3?
problems.idea: Express the short side in terms of the long side L.
steps: L(L-7)<60 factors as (L-12)(L+5)<0.
Combined with L>7, this gives 7<L<12.
Only 12.3 is outside that interval.

problems.title: Circumradius of a triangle inside a square
problems.question: A square has side 4. Join the midpoints of two adjacent sides to the opposite vertex. Find the triangle circumradius.
problems.idea: Choose coordinates for the three vertices.
steps: Take the triangle vertices (2,0),(0,2),(4,4). Its side lengths are 2√2,2√5,2√5.

problems.title: Append a digit to a whole number
problems.question: Append digit 2 to the right of positive integer a. Find the resulting number.
problems.idea: Appending a digit shifts the original digits left one place.
steps: Multiplying a by 10 makes a units digit of zero.
Add 2 to replace that zero with 2.

problems.title: Count squares symmetric in a coordinate axis
problems.question: How many squares have a vertex at (-1,1) and at least one coordinate axis as a symmetry axis?
problems.idea: Count each axis separately, then remove the overlap.
formulas: A square has two diagonal symmetry axes and two opposite-side-midpoint axes.
steps: For the x-axis as symmetry axis, reflection gives (-1,-1). These may be adjacent vertices, producing two squares, or opposite vertices, producing one. Thus there are 3.
For the y-axis the same reasoning gives another 3.
Exactly one square belongs to both groups: vertices (±1,±1).
The total is 3+3-1=5.

problems.title: The longer side from the diagonal vectors
problems.question: A parallelogram has diagonals 10,12 meeting at 30°. Find its longer side.
problems.idea: A side is half the sum or difference of the diagonal vectors.
steps: The larger squared side uses the plus sign.

problems.title: Triangle formed by absolute-value intercepts
problems.question: Find the area of the triangle made by y=|x-1|-3 and the coordinate axes.
problems.idea: Find its two zeros and its y-intercept.
steps: The y-intercept is (0,-2).
The horizontal base from -2 to 4 has length 6 and the height is 2.

problems.title: Use a marked root to identify a parabola
problems.question: The graph of y=-x²+(b-2)x+b+3 has a root at -2. A is the positive y-intercept, B the positive x-intercept. Find the area OAB.
problems.idea: Use the marked root to solve for b.
formulas: At a root, y=0; triangle area=intercept product/2.
steps: The parabola is -x²+x+6=-(x-3)(x+2), giving B=(3,0),A=(0,6).
The area is 3·6/2=9.

problems.title: Slope and intercept from two axis crossings
problems.question: Find k,b for y=kx+b through (5,0),(0,3).
problems.idea: The y-intercept immediately gives b.
steps: From 0=5k+3, obtain k=-3/5.

problems.title: A current slows a round trip
problems.question: A messenger can walk both ways between two riverside villages or row both ways. Walking speed equals the boat’s still-water speed. Which round trip is quicker?
problems.idea: The upstream delay outweighs the downstream saving.
steps: If 0<u<v, the boat time divided by walking time is v²/(v²-u²)>1.
Thus walking both ways is quicker. If u≥v, the boat cannot make the upstream trip at positive speed.
If u=0 the times tie. If mixing modes is allowed, rowing downstream and walking upstream is faster than walking both ways.
problems.answer: For the stated choice of one mode for both legs: walk, with a tie in still water.
problems.note: The answer assumes the same mode in both directions, as the alternatives state. A mixed-mode trip gives a different optimum.

problems.title: A rectangle diagonal is a circle diameter
problems.question: A rectangle is inscribed in a radius-6 circle and one side is 6 cm. Find the other side.
problems.idea: Its diagonal has length 12.
steps: The unknown side squared is 12²-6²=108.
The positive side is √108=6√3.

problems.title: Centres of a hexagon and an interior square
problems.question: A regular hexagon and an interior square share a side. Their centres P,Q are 2 apart. Find the hexagon area.
problems.idea: Both centres lie on the perpendicular bisector of the shared side.
formulas: Hexagon apothem=√3s/2; square centre distance to its side=s/2; hexagon area=3√3s²/2.
steps: Because the square is inside, the centre distance is (√3-1)s/2=2.

problems.title: One admissible root of a shifted square
problems.question: For which a does $|x-2|/(x-2)=(x-a)^2$ have exactly one real solution?
problems.idea: The left side is -1 for x<2 and 1 for x>2.
formulas: A real square cannot be negative; (x-a)²=1 gives x=a±1.
steps: There are no roots below 2; x=2 is undefined.
Exactly one of a-1,a+1 must exceed 2.
This requires a+1>2 and a-1≤2, giving 1<a≤3.

problems.title: Count worker-hours as the team grows
problems.question: Six workers need 10 hours for a job. They work from 11:00 to 17:00, then one worker is added each hour. When does the job finish?
problems.idea: Measure the job in worker-hours.
formulas: Work=number of workers·hours at equal productivity.
steps: The job needs 60 worker-hours. By 17:00 they have completed 6·6=36, leaving 24.
From 17–18, seven workers do 7; from 18–19, eight do 8. This leaves 9.
From 19–20, nine workers finish those 9 worker-hours.

problems.title: Range of a bounded rational function
problems.question: Find the range of y=3x/(x²+9).
problems.idea: Use a square to bound the denominator.
steps: Thus |3x/(x²+9)|≤1/2, with equality at x=±3.
The function is continuous on ℝ and attains both endpoints, so every intermediate value occurs.

problems.title: A rotated rectangle requires a direction
problems.question: A rectangle has AB=2,BC=5 as shown and is rotated 135° about A to AMNP, with B mapping to M. Find MC.
problems.idea: Use coordinates and state the rotation direction.
steps: Put A=(0,0),B=(0,2),C=(5,2). Under counterclockwise 135° rotation, M=(-√2,-√2).
Under clockwise 135°, M=(√2,-√2) instead, and MC²=(5-√2)²+(2+√2)²=33-6√2.
problems.note: The source sketch’s rotated labels and angle arc are incomplete. These answers use the usual correspondence A→A,B→M,C→N,D→P; a rotation direction must be supplied to choose one.
